comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides advanced technology and IP platforms for customers to design ASICs targeting AI, high-performance computing, and networking applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom provide custom, customer-specific silicon solutions, but they target different market segments and delivery mechanisms. AMD explicitly focuses on semi-custom SoCs for gaming consoles and handhelds (e.g., PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Steam Deck), whereas Broadcom offers IP platforms for customers to design their own ASICs for AI, high-performance computing, and networking. While both describe tailored hardware based on specific customer requirements, AMD's disclosed semi-custom products are integrated into final consumer devices by console manufacturers, while Broadcom's custom silicon is built to individual customer specifications for enterprise infrastructure applications.

sentences.text: AMD semi-custom SoC products power the Sony PlayStation® 5, the Microsoft ® Xbox Series S™ and X™ game consoles, as well as the Valve Steam Deck PC.

• Custom Silicon Solutions: We provide advanced technology and intellectual property ("IP") platforms for customers to design and develop application specific integrated circuits ("ASICs") targeting AI and high-performance computing, networking and storage applications. Our custom silicon provides the platform to integrate embedded logic, memory, serializer/deserializer ("SerDes") technology, IP cores and processor cores. ASICs are custom products built to individual customers specifications.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates for Intel focus on discrete client GPUs (Arc series) for PCs and a general xPU strategy, which contrasts with AMD's semi-custom console SoC business. Intel's disclosure does not mention participating in the semi-custom console SoC market with major gaming partners, nor does it describe tailored hardware for consoles in the same manner as AMD.

comparisons.peer_summary: GDDR is a high-performance memory solution optimized for high-bandwidth workloads in graphics cards, gaming consoles, and high-performance computing applications.
comparisons.comparison: AMD and Micron share a direct supply chain relationship regarding the gaming market, with AMD developing the graphics processing components and Micron providing the necessary memory. AMD’s semi-custom SoCs power gaming consoles like the PlayStation 5, which require high-bandwidth memory. Micron explicitly identifies gaming consoles as a key application for its GDDR high-performance memory, noting that GDDR is optimized for the high-bandwidth workloads encountered by graphics processing units, which are central to AMD's gaming solutions.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gaming products include GeForce RTX and GTX GPUs for desktop and laptop PCs, GeForce NOW cloud gaming service, and SoCs and development services for game consoles.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA provide system-on-chips (SoCs) and development services to game console manufacturers, establishing them as key hardware partners in the semi-custom gaming console market. AMD’s disclosure specifies its SoCs power the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and Steam Deck, while NVIDIA similarly identifies SoCs for game consoles as part of its gaming product portfolio, though it does not name specific console models in the cited text. Both companies leverage their graphics and processing technologies to create tailored solutions for the gaming market.
